# FilterButton

Filter button: opens or toggles a filter. It shows the filter's name, an optional count of what is applied, and a chevron when it opens a menu.

Also asked as: filter chip, filter control.

**Import:** `import { FilterButton } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterButton/FilterButton.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterButton/FilterButton.stories.jsx` — Overview, Metric, Appearances, Spacing, States, Selected, Disabled, Loading, HoveredState, PressedState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterButton/FilterButton.mdx`

## Usage

Use `FilterButton` for a control that opens a filter's options or toggles a
filter on and off, above a table or a list. For a value already chosen and
removable, show it as a `Tag` instead; `FilterButton` is the trigger, not the
applied result.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use the filter's name as the label: "Status", "Subject". | A verb phrase such as "Filter by status". |
| Use sentence case: "Grade level". | Title case or all capitals: "Grade Level". |
| Show the count as a bare number, only once a filter is applied: "Status 2". | "Status (2 selected)", or a "0" when nothing is applied. |
| Keep the name to one or two words. | A name long enough to wrap or truncate. |

## Best practices

### Keep space between filter buttons. {#keep-space-between-filter-buttons}

Leave a gap so neighboring filter buttons read as separate targets.

Do: A clear gap between filter buttons.
Don't: Filter buttons touching.

### Show the active count. {#show-the-active-count}

When a filter is applied, the trailing count says how many values are
active. Pass `trailingMetric` once at least one value is selected, and leave
it out when none is: `0` renders as a visible count of zero, not an empty
state.

Do: Subject shows its three applied values; Grade, with none, shows no count.
Don't: Subject has three values applied but shows no count.

```jsx
<FilterButton text="Status" trailingMetric={selected.length || undefined} />
```

### Let it hug its label. {#let-it-hug-its-label}

Keep the natural width, so the chevron stays right after the name. Filter
button has no prop to fill its container; don't stretch it across a wide row
with your own styles.

### Use the filter's name as the label. {#use-the-filter-s-name-as-the-label}

Do: The label is the filter's name.
Don't: A verb phrase repeats what the button already does.

### Turn off the chevron only when the button doesn't open a menu. {#turn-off-the-chevron-only-when-the-button-doesn-t-open-a-menu}

`hasChevronDown` defaults to `true`. Set it `false` only for a filter that
toggles directly on click, with nothing to open.

## Accessibility

- **A real button, unchanged.** `FilterButton` renders a `Button`
  underneath, so focus, activation and disabled/loading states all follow
  `Button`'s own contract.
- **The chevron is decorative.** It signals that a menu opens, but the
  accessible name comes from `text` and, when present, the applied count.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | string (required) | — | The filter's name. |
| `trailingMetric` | number or string | — | The count shown after the name. `0` shows; leave it out to hide it. |
| `hasChevronDown` | bool | `true` | The chevron that says a menu opens. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | — |
| `spacing` | enum | — | `default` draws 32. `compact` draws 24. |
| `isSelected` | bool | — | — |
| `isDisabled` | bool | — | — |
| `isLoading` | bool | — | — |
| `onClick` | func | — | — |
| `className` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `subtle`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

Anything not listed is not a valid value.
